title: 7 lead enrichment tools compared for B2B sales teams
summary: Compare 7 lead enrichment tools by pricing, features, CRM integrations, and automation. Find the right fit for your B2B sales workflow.
body_markdown:
Lead enrichment tools fill gaps in company and contact records, from missing work emails to job titles, company size, and technology used. The right choice depends on what your team already knows and what it needs to find.


If you have a spreadsheet of named contacts, you may only need their work emails. Building a target account list also requires finding companies and people. Revenue operations teams may need to keep CRM records current while protecting information that salespeople have already checked.


This guide compares seven lead enrichment tools for B2B sales teams, covering the information they need, their pricing, and the limits to consider.


## How lead enrichment tools work


An enrichment tool uses information such as a business email, company domain, or person’s name and employer to identify a record. It searches its supported sources for a match, then returns additional fields. Depending on the product, you can keep the results in its workspace, download a file, or update CRM properties.


Check the required inputs before uploading a list. A tool that needs a person’s name and company cannot find unnamed decision-makers unless it also supports discovery. Review the results to confirm they belong to the right person and current employer. Our guide to[how lead enrichment works](https://blog.floworks.ai/lead-enrichment/) explains the process and data-quality checks in more detail.


## How we compared these tools


We used official product pages, help documentation, and published pricing for this comparison. Prices were reviewed on October 29, 2026, and product documentation was checked through October 30. For each tool, we considered required inputs, returned data, delivery options, pricing, and limitations. We have not run a hands-on accuracy benchmark, so the order does not rank data accuracy or performance.


Floworks publishes this guide and makes Jesse. The recommendations explain where each product fits; none is a recommendation for every team. Prices reflect the billing terms shown and should be checked before purchase.

These prices cover different jobs and allowances. Compare what you need to complete the work: a discovery subscription, a CSV enrichment plan, and a CRM maintenance contract serve different purposes. The profiles below explain what each price includes.


## 1. Jesse by Floworks: company discovery followed by contact enrichment


Jesse suits teams starting with an ideal customer profile, or ICP. Describe the companies you want to find, search for people in relevant roles, and enrich the contacts you select. Its website lists work emails and profile links, along with company information such as technology and funding details. Consider it when you still need to build the prospect list.[Jesse product overview](https://agentjesse.ai/)


Pro costs $9 per month with monthly billing. It includes 1,000 monthly credits, CSV export, and email and phone enrichment. Searches and contact lookups consume credits at different rates, so those credits will not produce 1,000 complete contacts. Business costs $29 per month and adds API, MCP, and n8n access.[Jesse pricing](https://agentjesse.ai/pricing)


For CRM delivery, native HubSpot, Salesforce, and Zapier integrations are listed as coming soon. Plan to use CSV export or the supported developer connections. If your priority is automatically maintaining an existing CRM, assess the CRM-focused options in this list.


## 2. Apollo: enrichment within a prospecting workflow


Apollo is worth considering if you want prospecting and record enrichment in one platform. Its CRM enrichment works with Salesforce and HubSpot through manual, real-time, and scheduled modes. It can add contact, company, and technology information to matched records.[Apollo CRM enrichment documentation](https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/4413921630989-Use-CRM-Enrichment)


Before running enrichment, review the field mapping and controls for filling empty fields or overwriting values. Apollo’s documentation says manual enrichment overrides those configured settings. Test the action your team intends to use before applying it to records with verified information.


Full CRM enrichment access requires a paid plan. Check the seat requirements and credit allowance for your expected volume on[Apollo’s pricing page](https://www.apollo.io/pricing) .


## 3. Clay: configurable enrichment across multiple providers


Clay lets teams choose which fields to enrich and which providers to query. You supply the identifiers those providers need and configure the workflow. Its waterfall approach tries providers in sequence to find contact data, which is worth evaluating if one provider leaves gaps in your market.[Clay waterfall enrichment](https://www.clay.com/waterfall-enrichment)


Someone on your team will need to select providers, set up matching and validation, and maintain the workflow. Account for that work, including who will investigate failed runs.


Launch costs $185 per month with monthly billing and includes 15,000 Actions and 2,500 Data Credits. CRM integrations and automatic sync start on Growth, at $495 per month with monthly billing. Estimate both Action and Data Credit usage when working out how much volume a plan will cover.[Clay pricing](https://www.clay.com/pricing)


According to Clay’s FAQ, successful enrichment or validation can consume both an Action and Data Credits. Using your own provider API key avoids Clay Data Credits for that step but still consumes an Action. Calculate the cost of the full lookup and validation sequence, including any provider fees you pay separately.[Clay credit rules](https://www.clay.com/faq/do-unsuccessful-searches-consume-data-credits-what-about-actions)


## 4. Cognism CRM Enrichment: ongoing CRM data maintenance


Cognism CRM Enrichment suits teams that need to maintain existing CRM data. It combines a data-health review with enrichment and rules controlling which fields can change. The product includes phone-verified mobile data as well as company and contact information.[Cognism CRM Enrichment](https://www.cognism.com/enrich)


During an evaluation, ask to see what happens when someone changes jobs or when the product finds a value that conflicts with your CRM. Also check how it handles a contact who should no longer be used. These examples help you assess whether its update controls fit your team’s work.


CRM Enrichment starts at $12,000 per year and can be purchased separately or alongside Cognism’s prospecting product. This is the starting price for the enrichment product, not every Cognism package.[Cognism enrichment pricing](https://www.cognism.com/enrich)


Confirm the supported CRM, record types, and update rules in the package you are considering. Sending selected prospects to a CRM and maintaining records already in it are different capabilities. The annual starting cost is also a larger commitment than a small file-enrichment trial.


## 5. HubSpot data enrichment: enriching records where they already live


If you use HubSpot, check the native enrichment included in your subscription before adding another provider. HubSpot supports manual, bulk, automatic, and continuous enrichment of contact and company records. Its documentation lists eligible paid subscriptions and says core data enrichment does not consume HubSpot Credits.[HubSpot data enrichment documentation](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/records/get-started-with-data-enrichment)


Contact matching uses a person’s first name, last name, and work email. Company matching uses the company domain. You may need another process for records missing those identifiers.


Core enrichment has no separate credit charge under the eligible subscriptions, although you still pay for the HubSpot subscription. Smart properties and buyer-intent features have separate usage rules. Compare the supported properties with the fields your team needs to see whether native enrichment covers the gaps.


## 6. Lusha: contact-list enrichment through CSV and API


Lusha can add contact and company data when you already have identifiers for the people you want to enrich. Its enrichment page describes CSV, API, and CRM options. Matching inputs include a LinkedIn URL, a full name with company information, or an email address.[Lusha data enrichment](https://www.lusha.com/data-enrichment/)


For a spreadsheet workflow, check the plan that explicitly includes CSV enrichment. Pro includes CSV enrichment, API access, and webhooks. The annual-billing option reviewed costs $52.45 per month, billed yearly, with 7,200 credits granted annually and two seats included.[Lusha pricing](https://www.lusha.com/pricing/)


The pricing page lists one credit for an email reveal and five for a phone number. Some exports and API activity have separate charges. Estimate the steps your team will run, including moving the results into the destination system.


CSV and API access are on a different plan from the entry subscription. Check the volume limits and renewal terms for the plan that supports your workflow.


## 7. Dropcontact: work-email enrichment for known contacts


Dropcontact is an option when you know the person and company but need a work email. It does not sell a prebuilt lead database. Its documentation describes finding and verifying email addresses from existing identity information.[How Dropcontact uses existing contact data](https://www.dropcontact.com/help/does-dropcontact-sell-leads)


You can use file or API workflows for a list of named contacts. Its CRM integration suite is a separate subscription, so file/API credits do not include the CRM enrichment package.[Dropcontact pricing and product options](https://www.dropcontact.com/pricing)


At the 500-credit monthly setting reviewed, Files/API Starter costs €29 per month and Growth costs €35 per month. Growth adds enrichment fields; compare those with your requirements as well as the credit allowance.


Dropcontact distinguishes between finding a verified email and verifying an address you supply. Either can consume a credit under the stated conditions.[Dropcontact subscription rules](https://www.dropcontact.com/help/how-subscription-works)


If you have not identified the contacts yet, you will need a discovery step first.


## Which tools support automated lead enrichment?


To compare automated lead enrichment tools, check what starts a run and where the results go:


- Apollo supports scheduled jobs and automatic enrichment of eligible records after CRM sync. Its documentation says real-time enrichment does not guarantee instant updates.[Apollo automation documentation](https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/4413921630989-Use-CRM-Enrichment)
- HubSpot supports automatic enrichment for new records and continuous updates for previously enriched records. Administrators must enable and configure the settings.[HubSpot enrichment settings](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/records/get-started-with-data-enrichment)
- Clay supports recurring enrichment runs. Native CRM integrations and automatic sync are available on Growth and higher plans, and you configure the provider sequence and fields.[Clay plans](https://www.clay.com/pricing)


Jesse’s Business plan includes API, MCP, and n8n access for custom connections. These require setup; native CRM integrations remain forthcoming.[Jesse plans](https://agentjesse.ai/pricing)


Decide which fields an automated workflow may change and where uncertain matches should go for review. Test what happens to existing values and failed lookups before enabling it more widely. For products using AI, ask which step it handles and how you can inspect the result. Finding companies, researching a field, and matching records require different checks.


## How to choose a lead enrichment tool


Start with the records you have and the information missing from them. Write down what a salesperson needs to do next. A requirement such as “Find work emails for these named contacts and return them to this spreadsheet” gives you something specific to evaluate.


Follow the process from input to destination. Check that the tool accepts your identifiers and returns the fields you need. Then confirm how those fields reach your CRM or spreadsheet and how much manual cleanup remains. An API connection, CSV export, and automatic CRM update each involve different setup and ongoing work.


Use the same representative sample to compare shortlisted tools. Include the regions and company sizes you sell to, along with difficult records such as incomplete names or recent job changes. Count correct matches separately from populated fields.


For CRM workflows, check what happens to an existing value that someone has verified. Review duplicate handling and failed matches, and see whether a later run changes the result. Keep the original sample so you can compare the changes.


### Compare cost per usable record


Define what makes a record usable for your team. You might require a correct company match, a current role, and a work email that meets your validation standard.


Cost per usable record = total cost of the evaluated workflow ÷ records that meet your requirements


Include required subscriptions, usage charges, and separate provider fees in the cost. Track time spent on setup and corrections too. An advertised credit allowance does not tell you how many complete records your workflow will produce.

## Frequently asked questions


### Are there free lead enrichment tools?


Apollo documents up to 100 CRM contacts or accounts every 30 days on its free plan. When comparing free options, check whether the included enrichment and export features cover your workflow.[Apollo free enrichment allowance](https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/4413921630989-Use-CRM-Enrichment)


### Which tools should I consider for HubSpot or Salesforce?


Apollo documents enrichment for both CRMs. HubSpot users can also check which native enrichment features their subscription includes. With other providers, confirm the exact product and plan: exporting selected contacts to a CRM and updating existing records are separate requirements.


### How does waterfall enrichment work?


A waterfall queries data providers in a configured sequence. Clay is one option for building this process. Review the matching and validation steps as well as the provider order, and check that the returned data belongs to the right person and company.


### Is lead enrichment the same as email verification?


Enrichment adds information, such as a job title or work email. Verification assesses an address you already have or have just found. Some tools do both, but a verified email alone does not establish that the person still holds the role you want to contact.


## Choosing a tool for your team’s workflow


Consider Jesse or Apollo for new prospect discovery, and Clay for a configurable process across providers. If you need to maintain existing CRM records, compare your CRM’s native options with a dedicated enrichment package. Lusha and Dropcontact are worth evaluating for named contact lists that need work emails.


If you have an ICP and need to turn it into a company and contact list,[explore Jesse by Floworks](https://agentjesse.ai/) . Start with a focused search. Review the companies and roles it returns, then check the enriched contacts before using them in outreach.
